what: Biogen develops medicines for neurological disease. Its established business is multiple sclerosis treatments; its future depends on Leqembi for Alzheimer's, Spinraza for spinal muscular atrophy, and Skyclarys for a rare neurological disorder.
customers: Neurologists, hospitals, health systems and insurers worldwide.
money: Tecfidera, Tysabri, Vumerity and related products
biosimilar products and manufacturing for others
moat: Deep expertise in neurology and manufacturing for complex biological medicines, with rare-disease products that have few alternatives.
risks: Multiple sclerosis revenue keeps falling as older medicines lose exclusivity
Leqembi uptake has been slow because of the testing and monitoring Alzheimer's treatment requires
Revenue has been roughly flat for three years
It pays no dividend and return on invested capital is about 5%
opportunities: Gross margin of 76% means any revenue recovery flows through quickly
A subcutaneous form of Leqembi would make Alzheimer's treatment far easier to deliver
Cost cutting has protected profit while revenue stalled
watch: Leqembi prescriptions and the rate of decline in multiple sclerosis sales.
